note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Feeling hot and severe headaches; additional symptoms: palpitations, shortness of breath at rest (at desk), bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite, ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, decreased libido.
  - Symptoms largely occur at work; palpitations sometimes triggered when entering the elevator in the morning.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Began around time of changing jobs; ongoing.
  - Symptoms occur at different times (not all together).
- ENT symptoms (as applicable):
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: not reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: not reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: not reported.
  - Drooling: not reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: not reported.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: not reported.
  - Dyspnea: present at rest while sitting at desk; not with exercise.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): not reported.
  - Ear symptoms/hearing change: not reported.
  - Neck pain/swelling: not reported.
- Headache characterization:
  - Frontal; typically during work (meetings/laptop use); stays localized; sometimes mild nausea.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Denies prior similar headaches before this period; first time noticing hand tingling.
  - No prior ED visits/hospitalizations or injection therapies reported.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Medications: “thyroxine” (levothyroxine presumed); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Past medical history:
  - Patient reports “hyperthyroidism.”
- Social context:
  - Lawyer working in London; high job stress rated 7–8/10.
  - Alcohol: a couple of glasses of wine once weekly.
  - Tobacco: none. Recreational drugs: none.
  - Privacy/accompaniment: in a private space for tele-visit; accompaniment not documented.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: shortness of breath reported subjectively at rest (desk); no stridor/noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status/associated features: no dizziness/syncope reported.
- Vitals/exam findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Work-related stress/anxiety with possible hyperventilation causing palpitations, dyspnea at rest, and bilateral hand tingling; concurrent stress/ergonomic-related tension-type headaches. Possible thyroid dysfunction (including over-replacement) contributing to symptoms.
- Evidence summary:
  - Onset with new, stressful job; symptoms mainly at work (including elevator trigger), SOB at rest but not with exercise, frontal headaches during meetings/computer use, mild nausea, reduced appetite and ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, decreased libido. On thyroxine; patient states “hyperthyroidism.”
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with transcript):
  - Work-related anxiety/panic with hyperventilation (high): situational onset/triggers, SOB at rest (not exertional), palpitations, bilateral hand tingling, appetite/weight/libido changes consistent with stress.
  - Thyroid dysfunction, including iatrogenic hyperthyroidism (medium): on thyroxine; palpitations, feeling hot, weight loss, reduced libido; opposing evidence—symptoms largely situational at work.
  - Tension-type headache (medium): frontal headaches during meetings/screen time; high stress; limited migrainous features.
- Conflict noted:
  - Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” yet is taking thyroxine (replacement), creating uncertainty about thyroid status.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - In-person appointment to examine heart and lungs and assess overall status.
  - Order thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4 ± free T3) to evaluate for over-/under-replacement.
- Additional evaluations (consistent with DDx and transcript):
  - Measure vitals including blood pressure and pulse; consider ECG if palpitations frequent or exam abnormal.
  - Consider CBC and B12 if paresthesias or dyspnea persist or if exam suggests anemia/deficiency.
  - Screen for anxiety/panic (e.g., GAD-7) and review workplace ergonomics and stress management.
- Patient instructions:
  - Book in-person clinic visit via app as discussed.
  - Maintain regular meals and hydration during workdays; track symptom timing/triggers (meetings, elevator, screen use, caffeine).
  - Avoid new stimulants (excess caffeine/energy drinks) until evaluated.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Seek urgent care/ED if any of the following occur: worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, syncope, severe or “worst-ever” headache, new neurologic deficits, new throat tightness/voice change, stridor/noisy breathing, difficulty swallowing, or any facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling.
- Follow-up:
  - Follow up after labs and in-person exam to refine diagnosis and management.
  - Consider referral (e.g., behavioral health for anxiety management, endocrinology if thyroid dysfunction confirmed) based on results and clinical course.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Formal allergy list; medication dose/route/frequency; full ENT review (throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia, nasal/ocular symptoms), vitals, neurologic exam, caffeine intake, sleep history, workplace environmental exposure details, and ergonomic assessment.
  - Prior episodes of similar symptoms, prior imaging/labs, and any family history.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - “Hyperthyroidism” reported while on thyroxine replacement (conflict noted).
  - DDx includes environmental/CO exposure; no corroborating workplace exposure history in transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor pauses/hesitations; overall intelligible. No objective exam available due to tele-visit.
